$comment: Breed intake manifest — see README.md. roles: source material name → role name the tank reads (materials.ts). size: nominal body length relative to a minted fish (1 = FISH_LENGTH). motion: how the breed should move (wiggle = the tank's body wave).

betafish.notes: Minted: one model for every token of the breed (breeds/minted.mjs cut it from the 512 IPFS originals into paint regions, MINT-R<n>; MINT-EYE-R<n> where every token paints an eye cell). A token is this model plus its paint (breeds/minted/<breed>.json): the tank gives the shared geometry a per-token index and the token's own materials. Skinned (four bones; the authored Swim clip passes through). Each token's own texture atlas paints it (breeds/minted/atlas), so its UVs are kept and no face is merged.

angelfish.notes: Minted: one model for every token of the breed (breeds/minted.mjs cut it from the 512 IPFS originals into paint regions, MINT-R<n>; MINT-EYE-R<n> where every token paints an eye cell). A token is this model plus its paint (breeds/minted/<breed>.json): the tank gives the shared geometry a per-token index and the token's own materials. Flat authored colours. Rigged in Blender by rig/angelfish.py (the delivered model turned rigidly to face the rig convention, never edited), fluid throughout: a five-bone spine whose vertices blend by position (a travelling wave, a curve into every turn), three bones up each of the dorsal and anal fins (a ripple running back along them), and a streamer on each; the eyes rigid on the head. Kind asis: every face stays a whole voxel cell as drawn — a merged face meeting unmerged ones leaves T-junctions, hairline cracks that flicker as the skin bends (the eyes' 'line'). Clips swim, hover, burst, display and a bend dial. src/angel.ts drives them.

seahorse.notes: Minted: one model for every token of the breed (breeds/minted.mjs cut it from the 512 IPFS originals into paint regions, MINT-R<n>; MINT-EYE-R<n> where every token paints an eye cell). A token is this model plus its paint (breeds/minted/<breed>.json): the tank gives the shared geometry a per-token index and the token's own materials. Flat authored colours. Its node keeps the authored Swim clip (a slow bob and sway, the same on every token).

seaturtle.notes: Minted: one model for every token of the breed (breeds/minted.mjs cut it from the 512 IPFS originals into paint regions, MINT-R<n>; MINT-EYE-R<n> where every token paints an eye cell). A token is this model plus its paint (breeds/minted/<breed>.json): the tank gives the shared geometry a per-token index and the token's own materials. Flat authored colours. Rigged in Blender by rig/seaturtle.py (the delivered -30° rest yaw undone, rigidly; the model never edited): the shell, the head, two fore-flippers and two hind; clips swim, glide, look, paddle. src/turtle.ts drives them.

babyfish.notes: The babies of the metaquarium. Rainbow bands authored as primaryColor…primaryColor4 and secondaryColor, head to tail: each fish wears them as one candy-bright gradient between its two coats (VIVID-<n>); its stripe and mouth are sunny yellow on every fish (PAINT-#ffd23f), and a catchlight sparkles in each pupil (EYES-Sparkle). Rigged in Blender by rig/babyfish.py from the delivered source/babyfish.glb (never edited): head, body, two tail links and a forked fin as a soft spine (it bends as one piece), a fluttering dorsal fin, two blinking eyes; clips swim, zoom, wiggle, flip, peek and blink (wiggle_eyes, peek_eyes layer like a blink). src/babyfish.ts drives them.

blowfish.notes: A pufferfish and a flirt, rigged in Blender by rig/blowfish.py from the delivered source/blowfish.glb (never edited but for its eyes: each rebuilt as one white box and its pupil as one quad on its face, so a sliding pupil shows no seam). Already role-named. Everything hangs off a `puff` bone: the `puff` clip is a dial (its time is how puffed it is) that scales the fish round and stands its spines up from half tucked, so src/puffer.ts gulps it up, holds it and lets it go. Above it `body` carries the clips — swim, hover, gulp, zip, spin, flip, kiss, shimmy, bounce, spit, yawn, shy, wave, chomp — and the eyes and pupils are bones no clip moves: src/puffer.ts aims them, dilates them and closes them (true puffers can close their eyes).

crab.notes: Already role-named. The black mouth is EYES-Black coplanar with the body: the decal rule keeps it. Rigged in Blender by rig/crab.py from the delivered source/crab.glb (never edited): 23 rigid voxel parts — body, eye stalks, claw arms and jaws, two-segment legs — and the clips walk, idle, pinch, forage, wave, cheer. src/crab.ts drives them.

dori.notes: A blue tang, rigged in Blender by rig/dori.py from the delivered source/dori.glb (never edited; its GPU-instanced marking is joined and its doubled cubes dropped, and its Material.00x names, which collide in a shared .blend, are matched by colour and renamed to the roles the intake used to map them to; each eye is rebuilt as one white box and its pupil as one quad, so a sliding pupil shows no seam). The first breed that swims on its fins: a rigid body, two pectorals that beat like wings, a tail only for bursts, a dorsal that rises in a display; clips fly, hover, back, burst, pick, flare, headstand, flop. Its eyes are bones, not clips: src/dori.ts aims each one every frame (the box swivels, the pupil slides over it), and it never blinks — fish have no eyelids.

glowfish.notes: An anglerfish, rigged in Blender by rig/glowfish.py from the delivered source/glowfish.glb (never edited): the lower jaw, a head that flips open, a tail, two eyes that blink, and a three-link lure; clips swim, lure, chomp, blink. src/angler.ts drives them. The eyes glow rather than read as pupils, and neither glow role names a colour (nor contains 'eye', which the tank would read as an eye display): each fish draws its own. The teeth are metal.

hackerfish.notes: Half fish, half computer, rigged in Blender by rig/hackerfish.py from the delivered source/hackerfish.glb (never edited): the box, its screen, two paddle fins and a tail; clips swim, type, glitch. src/hacker.ts drives them. The glass and the face pixels are one display (SCREEN-): src/screen.ts draws faces, code rain and a boot spinner on it, the designer's face its neutral expression. No EYE material — eyeLife leaves it alone.

starfish.notes: The first breed drawn in-house, in our designer's style: rig/starfish-model.mjs writes source/starfish.glb voxel by voxel (whole cubes, one mesh per material, already role-named). The tips are GLOW-Tips (no 'eye' in a glow name), split one primitive per arm (splitByBone) so each is a small light riding its own tip. Rigged in Blender by rig/starfish.py, which never edits the model: the disc and its face, two blinking eyes, five arms in three rigid links each; clips crawl, idle, wave, stand, curl. src/starfish.ts drives them.

octopus.notes: Our second in-house breed: rig/octopus-model.mjs writes source/octopus.glb voxel by voxel in the designer's style (already role-named). Rigged in Blender by rig/octopus.py: a crown, a head and a breathing mantle, a siphon, eight arms of four links each (hinged underneath, blended at their joints), and eyes, pupils and brows that no clip moves — src/octopus.ts keeps each bar of a pupil level with the world, closes the lids, raises the eyes and the brows. Clips idle, crawl, jet, drift, tiptoe, wave, beckon, reach, peek, ink, pounce, sleep.

shark.notes: The heaviest source (28.8k tris): every voxel a whole cube, 26k of its faces buried — the intake culls them. Rigged in Blender by rig/shark.py from the delivered source/shark.glb (never edited), cut by position (its fins sit off the lattice): head, a dropping jaw ringed with metal teeth, eyes that roll back, pectorals, and a three-link tail for a true wave; clips swim, bite. src/shark.ts drives them. Big on purpose: the size follow-up gives it its length back.
